title: The Farmer and the Milk Pail

sentences.text: A farmer walked to market with a pail of milk balanced on one shoulder.
The road was long, so the farmer filled the quiet with plans.
I will sell this milk and buy a dozen eggs, the farmer said.
The eggs will hatch into chickens, and the chickens will bring a fine price.
With that price I will buy a new coat, and people will notice me when I pass.
The farmer pictured the coat so clearly that a proud little toss of the head followed.
The toss was small, but the pail was heavy and riding high.
It slid, tipped, and hit the road. Milk ran into the dust in a white stream.
There would be no eggs, no chickens, and no coat, because there was no milk left to sell.
The farmer stood still and watched the plan soak into the ground.
A traveler coming the other way offered a rag for the farmer's shoes.
I counted a coat I did not have, the farmer said, and I lost the milk I did have.
The farmer rinsed the empty pail at a roadside pump and turned back toward home.
Dreaming can be pleasant company on a long road.
Treating a dream as if it were already money is how a real pail ends up empty.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A traveler who buys every egg in town
Counting on a plan before the first sale is real
A coat that keeps milk from spilling
A pump that turns milk into chickens

questions.explanation: Every later plan depends on selling the milk. The milk spills, and the eggs, chickens, and coat disappear with it. That is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What is in the pail at the start?

choices.text: A dozen eggs
A folded coat
Milk
Chickens

questions.explanation: The farmer starts with a pail of milk. The eggs, chickens, and coat exist only in the plan.

questions.prompt: A proud little toss of the head is what kind of movement?

choices.text: A long drink from the pail
A slow walk back home
A careful count of coins
A quick upward movement

questions.explanation: A toss here is a quick throw of the head upward. That small movement is enough to unbalance the heavy pail.

questions.prompt: Why do all the plans fail at the same moment?

choices.text: They all depended on milk that spilled before any sale
The market refused to open that day
The traveler bought the coat first
The chickens escaped on the road

questions.explanation: The story never shows a real sale. Each step of the daydream starts with the milk. When the milk is gone, a reader can see that every later step had nothing to stand on.

questions.prompt: What happens last in the real events, not in the daydream?

choices.text: The farmer plans to buy eggs
The farmer turns back toward home
The pail hits the road
A traveler offers a rag

questions.explanation: The daydream comes first, then the spill, then the traveler. The last real action is rinsing the pail and turning back home.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
